item.title: Why Trump is campaigning in red states ahead of the general election
item.description: Many Americans say they're frustrated with the economy in recent polling. President Trump is campaigning in reliably red states as November elections draw near. Aaron Navarro has what you need to know.

item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.description: Some may think there's only one way to prepare a proper hot dog. Chef Farideh Sadeghin is here to prove that wrong with her cooking guide, "The Hot Dog Cookbook."

item.title: Alice Cooper on the evolution of his alter ego
item.description: Alice Cooper brings Anthony Mason backstage to one of his shows to talk about how he created his unforgettable alter ego ahead of the release of his new memoir, "Devil on My Shoulder."

item.description: The Ultimate Fighting Championship women's featherweight championship is on the line as Natalia Silva and Wang Cong meet in the UFC 332 main event. For the first time ever, the full main card will be simulcast on CBS and on Paramount+. UFC analyst Paul Felder breaks it down.

item.description: Lilia Luciano spoke to the attorney for Jane Doe, who says that campus police at Cornell University failed to properly investigate after she was allegedly raped at a fraternity house in 2024.

item.description: The Holei Sea Arch, located in the Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, was about 90 feet high before it collapsed.

item.title: G7 nations will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel to combat high prices
item.description: G7 countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products, starting with diesel. Joe Brettell, founder and principal of Forward Energy, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Makers of "Atonement" discuss their new film about a Marine and the first Iraq War
item.description: A new film, "Atonement," is based on the true story of a U.S. Marine who served in the first Iraq War. In the early days of the war he mistakenly fired on a family driving through a chaotic Baghdad intersection. Shots were being fired in many directions, but the Marine gunfire killed three civilians. The movie chronicles the Marine's long-simmering guilt and trauma and an elongated effort to reach out to the surviving family members in an attempt to find some manner of reconciliation. Reed Van Dyk, the film's producer and director, Dexter Filkins, who wrote the New Yorker story the film's script is based off of, and Boyd Holbrook, who stars in the movie, join "The Takeout" to discuss.
